architectural_units.name: User
architectural_units.description: Any individual or entity that interacts with the system, including donors and companies.

architectural_units.name: Security Service
architectural_units.description: Reverse proxy and load balancer managing HTTP/HTTPS traffic.

architectural_units.name: Traefik
architectural_units.description: Reverse proxy and load balancer tool used to implement the Security Service.

architectural_units.name: System Service
architectural_units.description: Core application service handling web rendering and business logic.

architectural_units.name: Next.js
architectural_units.description: Web framework used to build the System Service.

architectural_units.name: React
architectural_units.description: Library for building user interfaces within the System Service.

architectural_units.name: Data Service
architectural_units.description: Service providing relational database storage.

architectural_units.name: PostgreSQL
architectural_units.description: Relational database engine used for the Data Service.

architectural_units.name: Prisma
architectural_units.description: ORM tool used to manage database queries and schema.

architectural_units.name: Authentication Service
architectural_units.description: External service for user authentication.

architectural_units.name: Google OAuth
architectural_units.description: Third-party provider for user authentication.

architectural_units.name: Cloud Storage Service
architectural_units.description: External service for storing and retrieving files.

architectural_units.name: Amazon S3
architectural_units.description: Cloud storage provider used for file management.

architectural_units.name: Payment Processing Service
architectural_units.description: External service for handling payments and subscriptions.

architectural_units.name: Stripe
architectural_units.description: Third-party payment processing platform.

architectural_units.name: Analytics Service
architectural_units.description: External service for tracking and analyzing site traffic.

architectural_units.name: Google Analytics
architectural_units.description: Third-party analytics tool.

architectural_units.name: Error Monitoring Service
architectural_units.description: External service for tracking and managing application errors.

architectural_units.name: Sentry
architectural_units.description: Third-party error tracking tool.

architectural_units.name: Email Service
architectural_units.description: External service for sending and scheduling emails.

architectural_units.name: Brevo
architectural_units.description: Third-party email and marketing communication platform.

architectural_units.name: Docker
architectural_units.description: Containerization platform used to manage and run the system services.

architectural_units.name: Amazon EC2
architectural_units.description: Cloud infrastructure hosting the system containers.
The User interacts with the Security Service (Traefik) to access the system.
The Security Service (Traefik) routes HTTP/HTTPS traffic to the System Service.
The System Service communicates with the Data Service (PostgreSQL) using Prisma.
The System Service interacts with the Authentication Service (Google OAuth).
The System Service interacts with the Cloud Storage Service (Amazon S3).
The System Service interacts with the Payment Processing Service (Stripe).
The System Service interacts with the Analytics Service (Google Analytics).
The System Service interacts with the Error Monitoring Service (Sentry).
The System Service interacts with the Email Service (Brevo).

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The system is built as a collection of small, independent services (Security Service, System Service, Data Service) that communicate with each other and are managed as Docker containers.

patterns.name: Reverse Proxy
patterns.description: Traefik acts as an intermediary for client requests, redirecting incoming traffic to the appropriate internal services.

patterns.name: Load Balancer
patterns.description: Traefik distributes incoming traffic across multiple instances of services to improve availability and responsiveness.

patterns.name: Component-Based
patterns.description: The user interface is constructed using independent and reusable components that encapsulate their own logic, styles, and structure.

patterns.name: Observer Pattern
patterns.description: Used to establish a one-to-many relationship where objects (observers) subscribe to a subject to receive notifications of state changes, implemented via event listeners.

patterns.name: Singleton Pattern
patterns.description: Ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global access point to it, used here to manage the PrismaClient instance.

patterns.name: ORM (Object-Relational Mapping)
patterns.description: Technique used to convert data between the object-oriented programming system and the relational database, implemented via Prisma.
